statement: A top-10 economy legally authorises fully automated decisions (no human sign-off) in a new benefits, tax or immigration domain (official gazette; OECD.AI; by 2028-12-31)
status_at_phase_end: Not resolved. The clearest 2026 moves toward no-human-sign-off public decisions were in smaller economies (a Bloc C state enacted a general fully-automated-decision clause incl. discretionary matters; an Oceanian state widened automated benefit decisions). Among top-10 economies, one relaxed its general ADM rule (safeguards incl. human intervention on request), and another's federal government drafted an AI-in-migration law that expressly keeps the individual decision with staff; a sub-state draft there would allow discretionary automated decisions but is not enacted.

items.summary: A top-10 economy brought into force (SI 2026/82, 2026-02-05) a reform replacing its near-ban on solely automated significant decisions with a permissive regime (any lawful basis) subject to safeguards: information, representations, human intervention on request, and contestation. General, not specific to benefits/tax/immigration.
items.detail: Bloc G Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 s.80 in force 2026-02-05, new Bloc G GDPR Art. 22A-22D (Art. 22C safeguards). ICO draft ADM guidance consultation 31 Mar-29 May 2026; ADM code of practice Regulations SI 2026/425 (made 16 Apr, in force 12 May 2026).

items.summary: A sub-national jurisdiction in Bloc A enacted an automated-decision law covering public benefits and essential government services that grants a right to meaningful human review after adverse automated decisions (from 2027) - a move toward keeping humans in the loop.
items.detail: Colorado SB 26-189 'Automated Decision-Making Technology', signed 2026-05-14 (repeals/re-enacts SB 24-205). Sub-national; does not count for the indicator but signals direction in Bloc A states.

items.summary: A sub-national government in a top-10 economy proposed allowing fully machine-issued administrative decisions even where the authority has discretion, which would go beyond the national rule limiting automation to bound decisions. Draft only.
items.detail: Bavaria (Bloc D), draft 'Fünftes Modernisierungsgesetz', Art. 35 S.3 BayVwVfG-E, presented May 2026, in Landtag since July 2026. Federal § 35a VwVfG allows full automation only with explicit statutory basis and no discretion (existing bases: § 155(4) AO tax; § 31a SGB X social). Date approximate.

items.summary: The federal government of a top-10 economy tabled a bill on AI in migration administration that allows automated process monitoring and checks against public internet sources, but states that examination and decision in each case remain entirely with staff.
items.detail: Bloc D, Bundestag Drucksache 21/8275, 'KI-Migrationsverwaltungsgesetz (KIMVG)', dated 2026-09-30 (cabinet July 2026; first reading Oct 2026). New §§ 90d, 90e AufenthG.

items.summary: A mid-sized Bloc C economy (not top-10) passed a general administrative-procedure amendment allowing fully automated written decisions, including in discretionary matters, with only random checks, no named official, and a two-week objection right; ministries may designate domains by regulation, potentially including asylum. Precedent for larger economies.
items.detail: Bloc V, § 18a AVG and VStG amendment, National Council vote 2026-09-23; reported in force Oct 2026. Critics: epicenter.works / EDRi (2026-10-08). Not a top-10 economy.

items.summary: A small advanced economy (not top-10) rushed through a law widening automated decision-making for social-welfare benefits to 'any decision' under specified provisions; officials said it excludes generative AI.
items.detail: Bloc U, social security amendment widening MSD ADM powers (RNZ reports, 2026). Exact enactment date not verified; date approximate.

items.summary: No 2026 statute was found in Bloc A (federal), Bloc B, or other top-10 economies that newly authorises no-human-sign-off decisions in benefits, tax or immigration. Bloc B legal sources were not systematically searched in this backfill run.
items.detail: Searches covered Bloc A federal, Bloc G, Bloc D; Bloc B, Bloc N, Bloc O, Bloc E, Bloc F, Bloc P, Bloc Q not systematically checked. Pre-existing bases (e.g. Bloc D tax § 155(4) AO) are not 'new domains'.
